questions.stem: A historical case has sd 6 and n 9; what is the standard error?
questions.explanation: SE=6/sqrt(9)=2. The computation rests on divide by sqrt(n). Working backward through the relation confirms the value.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: Type one and type two errors
questions.stem: A historical case concludes an effect exists when it does not; what error?

options.misconception: names "Choice: No error" where the rule requires "Choice: Type I error (false positive)"
confuses false positive with false negative

questions.explanation: The type one and type two errors principle here is: False positive = type I. On that basis "Choice: Type I error (false positive)" is correct, while "Choice: No error" names "Choice: No error" where the rule requires "Choice: Type I error (false positive)".

questions.stem: A historical case has beta=0.05; what is power?
